transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

What finally pushed me to come in is that I’ll start an EPIC quality report, or sit down in a clinic metrics meeting intending to follow along, and within a few minutes my mind has wandered. Then I’m rereading the same numbers, or I realize I missed the whole point of what was discussed.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your attention and focus?
It’s been about two years and four months—since I was promoted and took on a much larger portfolio. The systems I used to rely on just started feeling overwhelming.
Did you struggle with your attention or focus back during your childhood or school years?

Yes. Even in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright but careless. I’d lose track of assignments or forget books at school, and my mother often had to sit with me while I finished homework so I could stay on it.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you have trouble sitting still or feel an inner urge to be constantly on the go?
I’m not sure I’ve really noticed that. I can sit through meetings; it’s more that my attention drifts than that I feel like I need to get up or move around.
Do these difficulties with focus and organization cause problems outside of work, such as at home or in your personal life?

Yes. At work, I’ve started missing or delaying clinic reporting deadlines, and other teams end up waiting on me. And I’ve had to step back from leading parts of the volunteer health workshops because I can’t keep the planning pieces moving reliably.
